answer_1.quote: We pick seven chitchat chatbots trained or finetuned on ConvAI2 ... to be evaluated in our experiments ... The framework can be used to rank a number of bots with little time and minimum human effort.
answer_1.outputs: Generated chatbot responses in multi-turn conversations.

answer_2.quote: We score each dialogue turn based on seven aspects: consistency, fluency, knowledge, specificity, diversity, relevance and proactivity ... We use the most widespread reference-free approach, perplexity, to evaluate the fluency of each generated turn. ... we use the average of Distinct-1 and Distinct-2 ... we use tf‑idf cosine similarity as the similarity function ... We also compare with four automatic baselines: PPL (perplexity), TA (token accuracy), BS (BERTScore).

answer_4.quote: We ask a group of human judges who are fluent in English to chat with each of the seven bots and then manually assess the ability of the bots. Seven dimensions, namely fluency, knowledge, proactivity, specificity, diversity, consistency, and relevance, are used to help them complete the ranking task which are rated on a 5-point Likert scale.
answer_4.guideline: Judges were trained with one positive and one negative example for each dimension and then asked to rate each bot on the seven dimensions (fluency, knowledge, proactivity, specificity, diversity, consistency, relevance) using a 5‑point Likert scale, as well as provide an overall ranking.
